question: An animal body that can be cut along its axis in any plane to give two identical parts is said to be
solution:
The question describes a body that can be divided into two identical halves by a cut made in any plane through the main axis.

That is radial symmetry. Think of cutting a cake through the centre: every cut gives two equal halves, and there are many such planes. Animals such as Hydra, jellyfish, sea anemones and adult starfish have this plan, which suits a life where food and danger may come from any direction.

Bilateral symmetry allows only one plane to give identical halves, because the body has a right and left side, as in humans and insects. Asymmetrical bodies, like the sponge, cannot be divided into matching halves at all. The vague word symmetrical is not a precise type, so radial symmetry is the accurate description.

question: In the kidney of mammals, the site of ultrafiltration is the
solution:
Ultrafiltration is the filtering of blood at high pressure, when small molecules are forced out of the blood while cells and large proteins stay behind.

This happens in the Bowman's capsule. A knot of blood capillaries called the glomerulus sits inside the cup-shaped capsule, and the blood pressure there is high because the vessel entering is wider than the one leaving. Water, glucose, salts and urea are forced through the thin walls into the capsule, forming the filtrate. The filtered material then flows down the tubule.

The uriniferous tubule and renal tubule (which includes the loop of Henle) carry out selective reabsorption of useful substances such as glucose and most water, not filtration. The loop of Henle only helps to concentrate the urine.

question: Which of the following is true in blood transfusion?

option.a: A person of blood group AB can donate blood only to another person of blood group AB
option.b: Persons of blood groups A and B can donate or receive blood from each other
option.c: A person of blood group AB can receive blood only from persons of blood group A or B
option.d: A person of blood group O can donate only to a person of blood group O

solution:
Blood groups depend on antigens on the red cells and antibodies in the plasma. Group A has antigen A and anti-B; group B has antigen B and anti-A; group AB has both antigens and no antibodies; group O has no antigens and both antibodies.

Because group AB produces no antibodies, it can receive blood from every group. But its red cells carry both A and B antigens, so it can be given only to another AB person, whose plasma has no anti-A or anti-B to attack them. That makes the first statement true.

Groups A and B cannot exchange blood, since each has antibodies against the other's antigen. AB can receive from A, B, AB and O, not only A or B. Group O is the universal donor, so it can give to all groups, not only to O.

question: Plant growth can be artificially stimulated by the addition of
solution:
Plant hormones control growth, and they are grouped into those that promote growth and those that inhibit it. The question asks for a growth promoter that can be added artificially.

Gibberellin is a growth promoter. It stimulates cell division and cell elongation in the stem, encourages seed germination and helps fruits develop. When sprayed on a dwarf plant, it makes the stem grow taller, so it is the hormone used to stimulate growth artificially.

Kinin (cytokinin) mainly promotes cell division in shoots and roots, but it does not cause the strong stem elongation described here. Abscisic acid is an inhibitor that causes dormancy and closes stomata in dry weather, and ethylene is a gas that hastens ripening, ageing and leaf fall. The last two would slow growth rather than stimulate it.

question: Organisms living in an estuarine habitat are adapted to

option.b: survive only in water with low salinity
option.d: feed only on phytoplankton and dead organic matter

solution:
An estuary is where a river meets the sea, so fresh water and salt water mix. This makes its most striking feature a constantly changing salt content.

At low tide the estuary is mostly fresh river water; as the tide comes in, sea water pushes upstream and salinity rises sharply. Organisms that live there therefore need special adaptations to withstand wide fluctuations in salinity. Many are euryhaline: they can tolerate both dilute and salty water, and they control the salt and water balance of their bodies by excreting excess salt or taking in more water.

Temperature does vary in an estuary, but this is not its defining problem. The water is not always of low salinity, so organisms cannot survive only there. The type of food available is also varied, so feeding is not limited to phytoplankton and dead matter.

question: The most likely first colonizers of a bare rock are
solution:
Colonisation of a bare rock is primary succession. The first organisms to settle there must survive with no soil, very little water and full exposure to sun and wind.

Lichens can do this. A lichen is a partnership of an alga and a fungus: the alga photosynthesises and makes food, while the fungus holds water and anchors the pair to the rock. Lichens grow extremely slowly but they can dry out completely and revive when wetted. They also release weak acids that slowly crumble the rock surface and, as they die, add the first organic matter, starting soil formation.

Mosses and ferns need at least a thin layer of soil and moisture, so they arrive later. Fungi alone cannot photosynthesise, so they cannot be the first self-supporting colonisers of bare rock.

question: The significance of a very large number of termites involved in nuptial swarming is to

option.a: provide birds with plenty of food
option.b: ensure their perpetuation despite predatory pressure
option.c: search for a favourable place to breed
option.d: ensure that every individual gets a mate

solution:
Nuptial swarming is the mass flight of winged male and female termites after rain. The swarm leaves the old nest and flies out to find a suitable place to land and start a new colony. A very large number takes part so that, even though birds, lizards and ants eat many of them, enough survivors remain to pair up, lose their wings and establish new nests.

The other options miss the point. The swarm does not exist to feed birds, and not every termite gets a mate or survives. The large numbers give the colony many chances to locate and settle in a favourable breeding place, so the correct choice is the search for a favourable place to breed.

question: The autonomic nervous system consists of neurons that control the
solution:
The nervous system has two main divisions for movement. The somatic system controls muscles we can move at will, while the autonomic system controls organs that work without our thinking about them.

The autonomic nervous system supplies smooth muscle, cardiac muscle and glands. It adjusts the heart beat, the rate of breathing, the movement of the gut, the size of the pupil and the flow of saliva and sweat. Its two branches, the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems, speed the heart up in danger and slow it down at rest.

The voluntary muscles, the tongue and the hands are all under conscious control, so they are served by the somatic nervous system instead. You can decide to move your hand or your tongue, but you cannot decide to stop your heartbeat.

question: Countershading is an adaptive feature that enables animals to
solution:
Countershading means the upper surface of an animal is dark while the lower surface is light, as in sharks, fish, frogs and many birds.

Sunlight normally comes from above, so it lights the back and leaves the belly in shadow. That difference in brightness makes the animal's rounded shape stand out. With countershading the dark back absorbs light and the pale belly reflects it, so the two surfaces look equally bright. From the side, the animal's outline seems to flatten and it blends into the background; seen from above it matches the dark water or ground, and seen from below the pale belly matches the bright sky.

The result is camouflage, which helps the animal stay undetected while it hunts or hides. It is not used to fight or warn enemies, and bright warning colours or courtship displays rely on being noticed rather than hidden.

question: The correct base pairing for DNA is
solution:
DNA is a double helix with two strands held together by pairs of bases, like the two sides of a zip. The pairing is fixed, so each base can join with only one partner.

The rule is:

  • Adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T), using two hydrogen bonds.
  • Guanine (G) always pairs with cytosine (C), using three hydrogen bonds.

The pairs are complementary because of their shapes and bonding points: a larger two-ring purine always fits a smaller one-ring pyrimidine. That is why A pairs with T, not with G or C, and why guanine pairs with cytosine.

The other options pair a purine with a purine or a base with itself, which cannot happen in the double helix. The first option gives both correct partnerships.

question: Use the diagram above to answer this question. The developing embryo is usually contained in the part labelled
solution:
The diagram shows the female reproductive system. The part labelled II is the uterus (womb): a thick, muscular bag with a soft lining in which a fertilised egg settles and the embryo grows until birth.

Fertilisation happens in the oviduct (labelled I), and the tiny embryo then travels down into the uterus. The ovary (III) releases the egg each month, while the vagina (IV) is the birth canal. The embryo is protected and nourished inside the uterus, so the correct label is II.

question: The process in which complex substances are broken down into simpler ones is referred to as
solution:
The question asks for the name of the process that breaks large substances into smaller, simpler ones.

Catabolism is the set of reactions in which complex molecules such as starch, proteins and fats are broken down into simpler substances like glucose, amino acids and fatty acids, releasing energy. The opposite process, building complex substances from simple ones, is anabolism. Together, catabolism and anabolism make up metabolism, the total of all chemical reactions in a living cell. Tropism is a directional growth response of plants to a stimulus such as light or gravity, not a breakdown process, so it does not fit the question.

question: The organ which is sensitive to light in Euglena is the
solution:
Euglena is a single-celled organism that lives in water and makes its own food using sunlight, so it must be able to find light.

The structure that senses light is the eyespot (also called the stigma), a small reddish spot near the front end of the cell. It detects the direction and strength of light, and the organism then swims towards it. The flagellum is the whip-like structure used for swimming, not for sensing light. The chloroplast carries out photosynthesis and does not detect light, while the gullet is a groove through which small food particles are taken in. Only the eyespot is a light-sensitive organ.

question: The organelles present in cells that are actively respiring and photosynthesizing are
solution:
The question asks which organelles are found in a cell that is both respiring and photosynthesising.

Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration. They release energy from glucose and store it in ATP, so they are very numerous in active cells. Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis, trapping sunlight to make food. A leaf cell that respires and photosynthesises therefore contains both organelles. Lysosomes and ribosomes are involved in digestion and protein building, the Golgi apparatus and endoplasmic reticulum process and transport substances, and the nucleus and centrioles control the cell and help in cell division. None of those pairs releases energy from food or traps light.

question: Taenia solium can be found in the
solution:
Taenia solium is the pork tapeworm, a flat, ribbon-like parasite that lives in the small intestine of humans.

Its life cycle needs two hosts. The adult worm lives in a person and its eggs leave the body in the faeces. When a pig eats food or water contaminated with these eggs, the larvae hatch and form cysts in the pig's muscles. A person then becomes infected by eating pork that is not well cooked. Cattle are the intermediate host of a related species, Taenia saginata, while goats and dogs are not normal hosts of this tapeworm. This is why the pig is the correct answer.

question: Which of the following describes a characteristic of arthropods?

option.a: The organism finds it easy to grow freely
option.b: The organism has a pair of jointed appendages
option.c: The body is not divided into a number of segments
option.d: The body is covered by chitin

solution:
Arthropods are animals with a hard outer covering and jointed limbs, such as insects, crabs, spiders and millipedes.

The correct characteristic is that the body is covered by chitin. Chitin is a tough, light material that forms the exoskeleton, protecting the animal and reducing water loss. Because this covering cannot stretch, an arthropod must moult (shed it) in order to grow, so it does not grow freely. Their bodies are clearly divided into segments, which makes the option saying the body is not segmented false. They also have several pairs of jointed appendages, not a single pair as the second option claims. Chitin covering is the only accurate statement listed.

question: Which of the following distinguishes a butterfly from a moth?

option.a: The wings of a butterfly rest horizontally but those of a moth rest vertically
option.b: Both are active during the day
option.d: The abdomen of a moth is fatter than that of a butterfly

solution:
Butterflies and moths are both insects with scaly wings, so we need a real difference between them.

The correct distinction is that the abdomen of a moth is fatter than that of a butterfly. Moths generally have stout, hairy bodies, while butterflies are slender and longer. At rest, most butterflies hold their wings vertically above the back and most moths fold theirs flat or horizontally, so the first option has the positions reversed. Butterfly antennae end in a small club while moth antennae are usually feathery or thread-like, so they are not similar. Many moths fly at night, so saying both are active during the day is also wrong.

question: Which of the following types of feathers is used for flight in birds?
solution:
Birds have several kinds of feathers, and each kind has its own job.

Quill feathers, also called flight feathers, are the large, strong feathers of the wings and tail. Each has a stiff central shaft with barbs that lock together to form a flat, firm surface. This surface pushes against the air and produces the lift and steering needed for flight. Down feathers are soft and fluffy and trap air to keep the bird warm. Filoplumes are tiny hair-like feathers that sense how other feathers are positioned. Covert feathers are small feathers covering the bases of the flight feathers. Only quill feathers have the strength and shape for flight.

question: The plants that grow in deserts or very dry areas are referred to as
solution:
The question asks for the name of plants that grow in deserts and other very dry places.

Such plants are called xerophytes; the prefix xero means dry. They survive where water is scarce by storing water in thick stems, having small or spiny leaves, a thick waxy cuticle and few stomata, all of which cut down water loss. Mesophytes are ordinary plants that grow in moderately moist soil. Hydrophytes are water plants adapted to live in or on water. Epiphytes grow on other plants, such as tree branches, without being parasites. Only xerophytes are specially adapted to dry desert conditions.

question: Which of the following is the simplest living organism?
solution:
The question asks which of the listed organisms has the simplest structure.

A virus is the simplest and smallest of them. It is not made of cells; it is only a piece of genetic material (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat. It cannot feed, grow or reproduce on its own and must use a living host cell to multiply. Paramecium, Amoeba and Chlamydomonas are each complete single cells with a nucleus, cytoplasm, organelles and a cell membrane, so they are far more complex. This is why the virus is regarded as the simplest organism, even though it lies on the border between living and non-living things.

question: Proboscis is a structure that is mostly found in
solution:
A proboscis is a long, tube-like structure used for sucking or tasting food.

It is found mainly in insects. Butterflies and moths have a coiled proboscis that unrolls to reach nectar, mosquitoes have a needle-like proboscis for piercing skin and sucking blood, and houseflies have a spongy proboscis for soaking up liquids. Tapeworms have no mouth or feeding tube at all; they absorb already digested food through the body surface. Amphibians such as frogs have a sticky tongue but no proboscis. Molluscs usually have a rasping tongue called a radula, not a proboscis. Insects are therefore the correct group.

question: The structural adaptation of desert plants for water conservation is
solution:
Desert plants must save water because rain is rare. The question asks which structural feature does this.

Spiny leaves are the answer. In plants such as the cactus, leaves are reduced to spines. A spine has a very small surface area and no stomata, so almost no water can escape through it, and food-making is carried out by the thick green stem instead. Broad leaves with many stomata would lose large amounts of water vapour during transpiration. Spongy mesophyll is a loose tissue inside ordinary leaves that lets gases move about, and prominent stomata are openings that increase water loss. Those three features would be harmful in a desert.

question: The long and sharp clawed feet of birds is an adaptation for
solution:
The question asks what the long, sharp, curved claws of birds are adapted for.

Feet of this kind belong to birds of prey such as eagles, hawks and owls. The toes are strong and the claws (talons) are sharp and curved, so the bird can grasp and hold prey tightly while it kills and eats it. The same shape also lets perching birds grip a branch firmly. Feet for crushing seeds are short and stout with a thick bill. Scooping mud needs long toes without sharp claws, as in ducks and waders. Tearing flesh is done mainly by the hooked beak, not by the feet, so grasping prey is the best answer.

question: During the manufacture of food by plants, which of the following organisms uses energy from the sun?
solution:
The question asks which of the listed organisms uses sunlight to manufacture food.

Anabaena is a blue-green bacterium (cyanobacterium) that contains chlorophyll and carries out photosynthesis, using energy from the sun to build food from carbon dioxide and water. The others do not use light. Sulphur bacteria obtain energy by breaking down sulphur compounds in a process called chemosynthesis. Nitrosomonas converts ammonia to nitrite and Nitrobacter converts nitrite to nitrate, and both capture the energy released by these chemical changes. Because those three depend on chemical energy rather than sunlight, anabaena is the only light-using organism listed.

question: Movement of minerals and chemical compounds within a plant occurs during
solution:
The question asks for the name of the process by which minerals and chemical compounds move from place to place inside a plant.

That process is translocation. Food made in the leaves, mainly as sucrose, and other dissolved substances are carried through the phloem to growing parts, storage organs and roots, while water and mineral salts move up through the xylem. Osmosis is the movement of water across a membrane from a dilute to a more concentrated solution, and diffusion is the spreading of particles from a region of higher to lower concentration. Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from leaves. Only translocation describes transport around the whole plant.

question: The enzyme that is present in the saliva is
solution:
The question asks which enzyme is found in saliva.

Saliva contains ptyalin, also called salivary amylase. It starts the digestion of starch by breaking it down into a simpler sugar called maltose, which is why bread tastes sweet when chewed for a while. Ptyalin works best in the slightly alkaline conditions that saliva provides. Pepsin is a protein-digesting enzyme produced in the stomach and it needs acid to work. Rennin is also made in the stomach of young mammals, where it curdles milk. Lipase digests fats and is produced mainly by the pancreas and small intestine. Only ptyalin belongs to saliva.

question: Plants that have special devices for trapping and digesting insects are
solution:
The question asks for the name of plants that trap and digest insects.

These are carnivorous (insectivorous) plants, such as the pitcher plant, Venus flytrap and sundew. They usually grow in soil that is poor in nitrogen and other minerals. They still make their own food by photosynthesis, but they catch insects with special devices, including slippery pitchers, snap traps and sticky leaves, then digest them with enzymes to obtain the nutrients they lack. Symbiotic plants live closely with another organism for mutual benefit, parasitic plants take food from a living host, and saprophytic organisms feed on dead and decaying matter. None of these traps and digests insects.

question: The process of transforming the chemical energy of cellular fuels into the high energy bonds of ATP in plants is
solution:
The question asks which process changes the chemical energy stored in food into the high-energy bonds of ATP.

That process is respiration. In respiration, glucose and other cellular fuels are broken down in a series of enzyme-controlled steps, and the energy released is used to join a phosphate group to ADP, forming ATP. ATP is the energy currency of the cell and powers activities such as growth, muscle action and active transport. Photosynthesis does the opposite: it uses light energy to build food and stores energy in glucose. Photolysis is only the splitting of water by light during photosynthesis, and autotrophism is the ability to make food from simple substances, not the release of energy from fuel.

question: Fungi are referred to as heterotrophs because they
solution:
Fungi are called heterotrophs because they cannot make their own food and must obtain it from other organisms or from dead matter.

The reason is that fungi lack chlorophyll, the green pigment that traps sunlight for photosynthesis. Without chlorophyll they cannot use light energy to build sugar, so they feed on ready-made food. Most fungi are saprophytes: they digest dead leaves and other remains outside their bodies and then absorb the soluble products. Being filamentous, having a mycelium and lacking roots describe their body form, but none of these explains their feeding habit, because a plant could have similar features and still make food if it had chlorophyll.

question: An example of a parasitic protozoan is
solution:
The question asks for an example of a protozoan that lives as a parasite.

Plasmodium is the correct example. It is a single-celled protozoan that lives as a parasite inside the red blood cells and liver cells of humans, causing malaria, and it is spread from person to person by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito. Paramecium is a free-living protozoan that feeds on bacteria in pond water. Euglena also lives freely in water and can make its own food using sunlight. Chlamydomonas is a free-living green alga. Only Plasmodium depends on a living host and harms it.

question: Which blood cells are involved in the immune response of vertebrates?
solution:
The question asks which blood cells carry out the immune response of vertebrates.

Lymphocytes are the white blood cells that recognise foreign substances called antigens and defend the body against them. B lymphocytes make antibodies that stick to antigens and help destroy disease-causing organisms, while T lymphocytes attack infected cells directly and help control the whole response. Erythrocytes (red cells) only carry oxygen. Phagocytes and monocytes can engulf germs as a first line of defence, but the specific, antibody-based immune response described in the question is the work of lymphocytes, so they are the correct answer.

question: The blood circulatory system of vertebrates consists of

option.d: Heart, vena cava, arteries and veins

solution:
The question asks what makes up the blood circulatory system of vertebrates.

It consists of the heart, arteries, capillaries and veins. The heart is a muscular pump that pushes blood around the body. Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure, capillaries are tiny thin-walled vessels where substances pass between the blood and body cells, and veins return blood to the heart. The aorta and vena cava are simply named examples of an artery and a vein, so options that list them in place of the general classes leave out the capillaries or the main vessel types. The first option gives all four classes and is therefore complete.

question: A plant tissue that carries water and mineral salts is the
solution:
The question asks which plant tissue carries water and mineral salts.

The answer is the xylem. Xylem is a woody tissue made of dead, hollow cells joined end to end. Water and dissolved minerals enter the root hairs and travel up through the xylem to the stem and leaves, pulled mainly by transpiration. The phloem is the other transport tissue; it carries food such as sucrose from the leaves to other parts. The cambium is a layer of dividing cells that produces new xylem and phloem, and the cortex is the packing tissue between the epidermis and the vascular bundles. Only xylem transports water and salts.

question: Which of the following helps in the clotting of blood?
solution:
The question asks which part of blood helps it to clot.

Platelets are the answer. They are tiny fragments of cells made in the bone marrow. When a blood vessel is cut, platelets stick to the damaged wall and to one another and release substances that start a chain of reactions. In this chain the soluble protein fibrinogen is changed into insoluble fibrin threads, which form a mesh that traps blood cells and seals the wound. Red blood cells carry oxygen, white blood cells defend the body, and plasma is the liquid that carries cells and dissolved substances. None of these forms the clot itself.

question: The part of the mammalian skin involved in excretion is the
solution:
The question asks which part of the mammalian skin removes waste substances from the body.

That part is the sweat glands. These coiled glands lie in the dermis and open onto the skin surface through pores. They produce sweat, which contains water, salts and a little urea, so waste is carried out of the body. As sweat evaporates it also cools the body, so the glands help in temperature control as well. The malpighian layer is the dividing region of the epidermis, the sebaceous gland produces oil that keeps skin and hair soft, and the horny layer is the tough outer layer of dead cells. Only the sweat glands carry wastes away.

question: Which of the following forms about 55% of the volume of the blood in man?
solution:
The question asks which component forms about 55% of the volume of human blood.

Blood is roughly 55% plasma and about 45% cells. Plasma is the pale yellow liquid part. It is mostly water and carries dissolved substances such as glucose, amino acids, salts, hormones, antibodies and urea, as well as all the blood cells. Erythrocytes (red cells), leucocytes (white cells) and platelets together make up the remaining cellular portion, which is smaller than the plasma volume. Of the options given, only plasma is a liquid and forms the larger part of blood volume, so it is the correct answer.

question: Which of the following is a waste product of an insect?
solution:
The question asks which substance is a waste product of an insect.

The answer is uric acid. Insects break down nitrogen-containing waste into uric acid, which dissolves only slightly in water, and pass it out as a dry white paste from the Malpighian tubules into the gut. Making a paste instead of dilute urine saves a great deal of water, which is an important adaptation for life on dry land. Alkaloids are plant chemicals, not insect wastes. Sweat is a waste product of mammals, and mucilage is a slimy substance produced by plants. Uric acid is the only insect waste listed.

question: The main structure in vertebrates that supports and protects the body is the
solution:
The question asks which structure supports and protects the body in vertebrates.

That structure is the skeleton. It is made of bone and cartilage and forms a strong framework inside the body. It holds the body upright, gives it shape and protects delicate organs: the skull protects the brain, the ribs protect the heart and lungs, and the backbone protects the spinal cord. Ligaments are tough cords that join bone to bone at a joint, muscles produce movement by pulling on bones, and a joint is simply a place where two bones meet. None of these can support and protect the whole body on its own.

question: The chitin in the exoskeleton of many arthropods is strengthened by
solution:
The question asks what strengthens the chitin of the exoskeleton in many arthropods.

The answer is calcium compounds. Chitin on its own is tough but fairly flexible. In many arthropods, especially crustaceans such as crabs, crayfish and lobsters, calcium salts are deposited within the chitin, making the shell hard and rigid enough to protect and support the animal. Lipids are fats and oils that would soften the surface rather than harden it, and organic salt is too vague to name the strengthening material. Proteins are also found in the cuticle and help harden it in insects, but the mineral strengthening that the question refers to is calcium.

question: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to a stigma is
solution:
The question asks for the name of the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma.

This transfer is called pollination. The anther is the part of the stamen that produces pollen, and the stigma is the tip of the carpel that receives it. Pollen may be carried by wind, insects, water or other animals. After pollination, a pollen grain grows a tube down the style to the ovule, where fertilisation takes place and a seed begins to form. Fertilisation is therefore the fusion of male and female gametes that happens later. Placentation is the arrangement of ovules inside the ovary, and propagation means producing new plants.

question: The male reproductive organ of a flower is the
solution:
The question asks which part of a flower is the male reproductive organ.

The male organ is the stamen. Each stamen has two parts: the anther, which produces pollen grains containing the male gametes, and the filament, a stalk that holds the anther up where pollinators or wind can reach it. The female organ is the carpel, made of the stigma, style and ovary, so carpel is the opposite of what is asked. Petals are the coloured parts that attract pollinators, and sepals are the small green parts that protect the flower bud. Only the stamen produces male gametes.

question: The gland that is found just below the hypothalamus is the
solution:
The question asks which gland lies just below the hypothalamus.

That gland is the pituitary gland. It is a small, pea-sized gland attached to the hypothalamus by a short stalk at the base of the brain, and the hypothalamus controls it through hormones and nerve signals. The pituitary is called the master gland because the hormones it releases, such as growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone and antidiuretic hormone, control other glands and many body processes. The thyroid and parathyroid lie in the neck, and the adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys, so neither is below the hypothalamus.

question: The most important plant hormone is
solution:
The question asks which plant hormone is the most important.

Auxin is the answer expected. It is the main growth hormone of plants. It is made at the tips of shoots and roots and causes cells to elongate. Auxin is responsible for phototropism, the bending of a shoot towards light, and geotropism, the downward growth of roots. It also helps cuttings to form roots and encourages fruit development. Cytokinin promotes cell division, gibberellin promotes stem elongation and seed germination, and abscisic acid causes dormancy and the closing of stomata. All are useful, but auxin is the principal hormone of growth.

question: The sensory cell that responds to dim light is referred to as the
solution:
The question asks which sensory cell in the eye responds to dim light.

The answer is the rod. The retina at the back of the eye contains two kinds of light-sensitive cells, rods and cones. Rods contain the pigment rhodopsin, which is very sensitive to low light, so they let us see in a dark room or at dusk. They do not detect colour, which is why things look grey in dim light. Cones need bright light and are responsible for colour vision and sharp detail. The lens focuses light onto the retina and the iris controls the size of the pupil, but neither is a sensory cell.

question: The absence of anti-diuretic hormone in humans results in
solution:
The question asks what happens when antidiuretic hormone (ADH) is absent.

ADH is released from the pituitary gland and acts on the kidneys. It makes the collecting ducts of the nephrons more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed into the blood and less is lost in urine. When ADH is absent, the ducts stay almost waterproof, very little water is reabsorbed, and large volumes of dilute urine are produced. The body then loses water faster than it takes it in, so dehydration increases. The other options claim that dehydration is reduced or removed, which is the opposite of the truth. This condition is known as diabetes insipidus.

question: Oestrogen is a hormone that is synthesized in the
solution:
The question asks where the hormone oestrogen is made.

Oestrogen is synthesized in the ovaries, the female reproductive organs. It is produced by the cells of the ovarian follicles as they grow, and its level rises during the menstrual cycle. Oestrogen causes the lining of the uterus to thicken, develops and maintains female secondary sexual characteristics such as breast development, and helps control the release of eggs. The testes produce testosterone, the anterior pituitary produces FSH and LH, and the adrenal cortex makes cortisol with only small amounts of sex hormones. The main source of oestrogen is the ovary.

question: The eye defect caused by the development of cloudy areas in the lens is
solution:
The question asks which eye defect is caused by cloudy areas developing in the lens.

The answer is cataract. The lens is normally clear and focuses light on the retina. In a cataract, proteins in the lens break down and clump together, so the lens becomes cloudy or milky. Light is then scattered instead of being sharply focused, and vision becomes blurred while colours look dull. It is common in old age and can be treated by replacing the lens with a clear artificial one. Presbyopia is the loss of near focus with age, glaucoma is caused by high pressure inside the eye, and astigmatism is caused by an unevenly curved cornea or lens.

question: A pollutant that is biodegradable is
solution:
The question asks which pollutant can be broken down by living organisms, that is, is biodegradable.

Sewage is the answer. Sewage contains human waste, food remains and other organic matter. Bacteria and other decomposers break these materials down into simple harmless substances such as water, carbon dioxide and mineral salts, so the waste is gradually removed. Heavy metals such as lead and mercury are never broken down by organisms, and cellophane and plastics also decompose very slowly or not at all, so they remain in the environment for a long time. Crude oil can be attacked by some bacteria, but only very slowly, whereas sewage is readily biodegradable.

question: A tropical disease caused by Trypanosoma is
solution:
The question asks which tropical disease is caused by Trypanosoma.

The answer is sleeping sickness, also called trypanosomiasis. Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan that lives in the blood and tissue fluids of humans and other animals, and it is spread by the bite of the tsetse fly. The infection causes fever, headache, weakness and swollen lymph nodes, and when the parasite reaches the brain it causes confusion, disturbed sleep and eventually coma. River blindness is caused by a worm spread by blackflies, yellow fever is caused by a virus spread by mosquitoes, and malaria is caused by Plasmodium. Only sleeping sickness is caused by Trypanosoma.

question: The solid part of the ecosystem is referred to as the
solution:
The question asks for the name of the solid part of the ecosystem.

That part is the lithosphere, which means the rocky, solid outer layer of the earth, including soil, rocks and minerals. It is the ground in which plants are rooted and where many animals live and burrow. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth, the hydrosphere is all the water on the earth's surface, and the biosphere is the whole zone of living things together with the parts they inhabit. Only the lithosphere refers to the solid, non-liquid and non-gaseous portion.

question: Which of the following is caused by Treponema pallidum?
solution:
The question asks which disease is caused by Treponema pallidum.

The answer is syphilis. Treponema pallidum is a spiral-shaped bacterium, known as a spirochaete. It is usually passed from one person to another during sexual contact and enters through small breaks in the skin or moist membranes. The first sign is a painless sore, and if the infection is not treated it later damages the skin, bones, heart and brain. Gonorrhoea is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, leprosy by Mycobacterium leprae, and tuberculosis by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Each disease has its own causative organism, so only syphilis matches Treponema pallidum.

question: The lowest level of organization in living organisms is
solution:
This question asks for the simplest level at which living matter is organised. The cell is the basic unit of life: it is the smallest structure that can carry out all life processes on its own, such as feeding, respiring and reproducing.

The levels of organisation build up in this order: cell → tissue (a group of similar cells) → organ (different tissues working together) → system (organs working together) → organism. A tissue is already made of cells, and organs and systems are higher still, so none of them can be the lowest level. Organelles such as mitochondria are parts of a cell, not levels above it, so the cell is the correct answer.

question: Which of the following is the most complex according to their cellular level of organization?
solution:
The question asks which item is built from the greatest number of different cell and tissue levels. A heart is an organ. It is made of several tissues — cardiac muscle, nerve tissue, connective tissue and blood — working together, so it stands at the organ level.

  • Euglena is a single cell; it carries out all life processes but has no tissues.
  • Hydra is multicellular, yet it has only two cell layers and no true organs.
  • Hair is mostly dead keratinised material, not a living organ.

Since an organ is the highest level present among the choices, the heart is the most complex.

question: Which of the following organisms is multicellular?
solution:
The question asks which organism is made of many cells. Spirogyra is a green alga that grows as a long filament of many identical cylindrical cells joined end to end, so it is multicellular.

The other three are single-celled (unicellular) organisms. Chlamydomonas is a one-celled green alga with two flagella, Amoeba is a one-celled protozoan that moves with pseudopodia, and Euglena is a one-celled flagellated organism. Each of them carries out all life activities inside a single cell, so none shows the division of labour between cells that a multicellular body has.

question: In bryophytes, sex organs are produced in the
solution:
Bryophytes such as mosses and liverworts have a life cycle in which the green leafy plant we see is the gametophyte. This haploid stage produces the sex organs: the antheridia, which make sperms, and the archegonia, each containing an egg cell. Water is needed for the sperm to swim to the egg.

After fertilisation the zygote grows into the sporophyte, the stalked capsule that produces spores by meiosis. The protonema is the young thread-like gametophyte that grows from a spore, and rhizoids are root-like hairs that anchor the plant. Neither of these bears sex organs, so the gametophyte is the correct answer.

question: Seed plants are the most dominant vegetation on land because of
solution:
Seed plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) cover most of the land because of efficient seed dispersal. A seed contains an embryo with stored food and a protective coat, so it can survive harsh conditions and be carried far by wind, water or animals. This lets the plant spread into new areas without needing water for fertilisation.

  • Motile gametes belong to lower plants such as mosses and ferns, which must have water for the sperm to swim.
  • Photosynthesis is carried out by all green plants, so it does not explain dominance.
  • Water availability is a limiting factor on land, not an advantage.

The seed habit is therefore the main reason for their success.

question: Which of the following is an arboreal organism?
solution:
An arboreal organism is one that lives in or on trees. Among the options, the bird is arboreal: it perches, nests, roosts and feeds in trees, and its wings, light body and grasping feet suit this life.

An elephant and an antelope are large terrestrial animals that walk on the ground and feed on low vegetation, while a fish lives in water and breathes with gills. None of those three is adapted to life in the canopy, so the bird is the only correct choice.

question: A dental formula is given as i 21, c 00, pm 32, m 33. The general formula above represents that of
solution:
A dental formula lists the number of each kind of tooth on one side of the upper and lower jaws, written as upper over lower. Reading the formula:

  • Incisors 2/1 — used for nipping grass.
  • Canines 0/0 — none, leaving a gap called the diastema.
  • Premolars 3/2 and molars 3/3 — broad, flat grinding teeth.

The upper jaw has 8 teeth on each side and the lower jaw has 6, giving 28 teeth in all. Large canines are missing and there are many flat cheek teeth, which is the pattern of a herbivore such as a rabbit. A carnivore has big pointed canines and fewer grinders, an omnivore has a mixture of both, and a detritus feeder eats decaying matter rather than chewing vegetation.

question: A circulatory system is very essential in mammals but not in smaller organisms like Amoeba because

option.b: Diffusion is sufficient to transport materials in Amoeba

solution:
Mammals are large, so their surface area is small compared with their volume. Oxygen and food would take far too long to reach deep tissues by diffusion alone, so a circulatory system pumps blood that carries materials quickly to every cell.

Amoeba is a single microscopic cell, so its surface area is very large relative to its volume. Oxygen diffuses in through the cell membrane and carbon dioxide diffuses out, while digested food spreads through the cytoplasm. This makes diffusion sufficient to transport materials in Amoeba. Living in fresh water is not the reason, lacking haemoglobin is irrelevant to the need for transport, and Amoeba respires aerobically, not anaerobically.

question: In vascular plants, the sieve tubes and companion cells are present in the
solution:
The question asks where sieve tubes and companion cells are found. Both are conducting tissues of the phloem, the tissue that transports dissolved sugars, mainly sucrose, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

Sieve tubes are columns of living cells joined end to end, with perforated end walls called sieve plates, and they carry the food. Each sieve tube has a companion cell beside it, linked by fine pores; the companion cell supplies the energy and proteins the sieve tube has lost. The xylem carries water and mineral salts using vessels and tracheids. The cambium is a meristem that produces new xylem and phloem, and the cortex is packing tissue. The answer is therefore phloem.

question: The stomata of leaves are similar in function to the
solution:
Stomata are tiny pores on the leaf surface, opened and closed by guard cells, through which carbon dioxide enters and oxygen and water vapour leave.

Their closest equivalent is the spiracle of insects: small openings along the sides of an insect's body that let air into the tracheae for gas exchange and can be closed to reduce water loss. A pharynx is the passage behind the mouth, not a gas pore. Fish scales are protective plates, and the trachea of a toad is a single tube leading to the lungs rather than an external opening. Only the spiracle matches the stomata in structure and function.

question: The use of moist skin for respiration in amphibians is known as
solution:
Cutaneous means relating to the skin. Amphibians such as frogs and toads have thin, moist skin with a rich blood supply, and oxygen enters while carbon dioxide leaves through it. This is cutaneous respiration, breathing through the skin.

  • Pulmonary respiration is breathing with the lungs.
  • Buccal respiration is gas exchange across the moist lining of the mouth.
  • Cellular respiration is the chemical breakdown of food inside cells to release energy, not a way of taking in oxygen from outside.

The phrase moist skin in the question points directly to the skin, making cutaneous respiration the correct choice.

question: Water in plants is removed as water vapour through the process of
solution:
Transpiration is the loss of water as vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata of the leaves. Water evaporates from the moist surfaces of the mesophyll cells into the air spaces, then diffuses out through the stomatal pores. This creates a pull that draws water up the xylem from the roots and it also cools the leaf.

Diffusion and osmosis move molecules or water across membranes but do not describe the loss of vapour from a whole plant. Evaporation is the physical change of liquid water to vapour; it is only one step inside transpiration, but the biological process by which a plant loses water vapour has its own name, transpiration.

question: An example of an organ of perennation in plants is
solution:
A perennating organ lets a plant live through an unfavourable season, such as a long dry season, and grow again afterwards. A rhizome is an underground stem swollen with stored food. It survives the dry period, then sends up new leafy shoots and roots when conditions improve.

  • A seed is a reproductive unit for dispersal and a new plant, not the usual meaning of a perennating organ.
  • Petals and the calyx are flower parts that wither and fall after flowering.

Other perennating organs include bulbs, corms and tubers, which are modified stems or roots that store food. The rhizome is therefore the example required.

question: Alternation of generations is a feature shown in
solution:
Alternation of generations means a life cycle in which a haploid gamete-producing stage alternates with a diploid spore-producing stage. Mosses show this clearly: the leafy green gametophyte makes gametes, and after fertilisation the dependent sporophyte capsule makes spores by meiosis.

Fungi do not form gametes and spores in this plant-type alternation. Grasses and conifers are seed plants whose gametophytes are tiny and stay inside the flower or cone, so there is no visible alternation between two free-living plants. Mosses, being bryophytes, remain the standard example of the phenomenon.

question: Coordination and regulation of body activities in mammals are achieved by the
solution:
Body activities are controlled by two systems working together. Nerves carry electrical impulses very quickly and produce short-lived responses, such as pulling your hand from a hot pot. Hormones are chemicals released into the blood by endocrine glands; they act more slowly but their effects last much longer, controlling growth, reproduction and blood sugar.

Neither system alone controls everything: a response may start with a nerve impulse and be sustained by a hormone, as in the fight-or-flight reaction. Muscles are effectors that carry out movement, not controllers. Coordination and regulation therefore need both nerves and hormones.

question: The cerebellum of the brain controls
solution:
The cerebellum is the rounded part at the back of the brain, below the cerebrum. It receives information from muscles and from the ears and coordinates muscular activity: it keeps movements smooth, maintains balance and posture, and stores the patterns for learned skills such as cycling or writing.

  • Reflex actions are handled mainly by the spinal cord and medulla.
  • Emotional expression is controlled by the limbic system and the cerebrum.
  • The endocrine system is regulated by the hypothalamus and pituitary gland.

A person with damage to the cerebellum moves clumsily and staggers, which shows its role in coordinating muscles.

question: The part of the brain responsible for peristalsis is the
solution:
Peristalsis is the wave of involuntary muscular contraction that pushes food along the gut. The medulla oblongata, at the base of the brain just above the spinal cord, contains the centres that control involuntary activities: breathing, heart beat, the width of blood vessels, swallowing and peristalsis.

The olfactory lobe deals with smell. The hypothalamus controls body temperature and water balance and links the nervous system to the pituitary gland. The thalamus is a relay station that passes sensory impulses to the cerebrum. None of these controls the muscular movements of the gut, so the medulla is the right answer.

question: Which of the following instruments is used for measuring atmospheric pressure?
solution:
Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air pressing down on the earth's surface. A barometer measures this pressure, and meteorologists read falling or rising values to forecast storms or fair weather.

  • A hydrometer measures the relative density of a liquid.
  • A hygrometer measures the amount of water vapour, that is the humidity, in the air.
  • A thermometer measures temperature.

Only the barometer is designed for pressure, so it is the correct instrument. The similar-sounding hydrometer and hygrometer measure quite different things.

question: The influence of soil on organisms in a habitat is referred to as
solution:
Environmental factors are grouped by their origin. Edaphic factors are those that come from the soil — its texture, pH, water content, mineral nutrients, humus and air spaces — and they strongly affect the plants and soil animals living there.

  • Physiographic or topographic factors are features of the landform such as slope, altitude and relief.
  • Biotic factors are the living parts of the habitat, such as predators, competitors and decomposers.

Since the question specifically names the influence of soil, the correct term is edaphic.

question: The genetic make-up of an organism is described as
solution:
The genotype is the complete set of genes, or alleles, that an organism carries in its cells, for example Tt or TT for plant height. It is the inherited instruction written in the DNA.

  • The phenotype is the outward appearance produced when the genotype is expressed in a particular environment.
  • An allele is one alternative form of a gene, such as T or t.
  • A chromosome is the thread-like structure of DNA and protein that carries many genes.

Because the question asks for the genetic make-up itself, genotype is the correct answer.

question: The major limiting factors of productivity in the aquatic habitat include the following except
solution:
A limiting factor is a resource or condition in short supply that holds down the growth and productivity of organisms. In an aquatic habitat the organisms are surrounded by water, so water itself is never scarce and cannot limit production.

The real limiting factors are:

  • Food and dissolved mineral nutrients, which may be used up quickly.
  • Temperature, which affects enzyme activity and therefore growth.
  • Sunlight, which decreases with depth and limits photosynthesis by floating plants.

Dissolved oxygen and salinity can also limit life. The one factor that is always present is water, so it is the exception asked for.

question: Which of the following groups of organisms feeds directly on green plants?
solution:
Green plants are producers: they trap sunlight and make food by photosynthesis. The organisms that feed directly on them are herbivores, also called primary consumers, and they form the second trophic level of a food chain.

  • Secondary consumers are carnivores that eat the primary consumers.
  • Producers are the green plants themselves, so they cannot feed on plants.
  • Decomposers break down dead remains and wastes, not living plants.

A grasshopper eating grass, or cattle grazing, illustrates primary consumers, which is the correct group.

question: A characteristic feature of tropical rainforest is that it

option.b: contains a large number of plant species
option.d: has a total annual rainfall of less than 50 cm

solution:
The tropical rainforest is the wettest and richest land habitat. It has heavy rainfall throughout the year, high temperature and humidity, and a very large number of plant species growing at different heights: an emergent layer, a canopy, understorey shrubs and ground herbs.

  • Trees here have broad leaves to catch light, not narrow ones; narrow, thorny leaves belong to dry areas.
  • Annual rainfall is well above 150 cm, far more than 50 cm.
  • Fewer plant species and low rainfall describe savanna or desert, not rainforest.

High species diversity is the characteristic feature asked for.

question: The study of how and why population size changes over time is
solution:
Population dynamics is the study of how and why the size and structure of a population change over time. Ecologists examine birth rate, death rate, immigration and emigration, and the age distribution, to explain growth, decline or stability.

  • Population estimation is simply measuring population size, using quadrats or the capture-recapture technique.
  • Population ecology is the wider study of populations in relation to their environment.
  • A population cycle is the repeated rise and fall in numbers shown by some species.

Because the question stresses change in size over time, population dynamics is the best answer.

question: A severe and long dry season is a characteristic feature of
solution:
The Sahel savanna is the dry belt just south of the Sahara. It has a very short rainy season and a long, severe dry season, so the vegetation is sparse: mainly grasses, acacia and thorny shrubs with small leaves and deep roots.

The Sudan savanna has a longer rainy season and taller grasses, the Guinea savanna is wetter still with more trees, and mangrove swamps are muddy coastal wetlands flooded by tides. Since the question describes a severe and long dry season, the Sahel is the correct habitat.

question: Which of the following is a nitrogen-fixing blue-green algae of soil?
solution:
Anabaena is a filamentous blue-green alga, that is a cyanobacterium. It holds the enzyme nitrogenase in special thick-walled cells called heterocysts, where it changes atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia the plant can use. It lives freely in soil and water and also inside the water-fern Azolla, enriching paddy fields.

  • Rhizobium is a bacterium, not a blue-green alga, although it fixes nitrogen in legume root nodules.
  • Nitrosomonas is a nitrifying bacterium that turns ammonia into nitrite.
  • Clostridium is a soil bacterium, not a blue-green alga.

Only Anabaena fits the description.

question: The soil with the highest water-retaining capacity is
solution:
Water retention depends on particle size. Clayey soil has the smallest particles, so the spaces between them are extremely fine. Water is held tightly by adhesion and drains away very slowly, giving clay the highest water-retaining capacity, although clay is poorly aerated.

  • Sandy soil has large particles and big air spaces, so water drains through quickly and little is retained.
  • Stony soil is mostly gravel and also drains fast.
  • Loamy soil is a balanced mixture that holds water well, but less than clay.

Clay therefore retains the most water.

question: The causative agent of poliomyelitis is
solution:
Poliomyelitis, or polio, is caused by the poliovirus, a small RNA virus that enters by the mouth, multiplies in the gut and may travel to the spinal cord, where it destroys motor neurons and causes paralysis, especially in children.

Fungi cause diseases such as ringworm and athlete's foot, protozoans cause malaria and amoebic dysentery, and bacteria cause cholera and tuberculosis. None of these causes polio. Antibiotics work against bacteria but have no effect on viruses, while polio is prevented by vaccination. This confirms that the causative agent is a virus.

question: One of the ways of controlling noise pollution in urban areas is

option.a: by siting industries away from residential areas
option.b: that fuel should be completely combusted by engines
option.c: by planting trees on both sides of the road

solution:
Noise pollution is unwanted sound that harms hearing and causes stress. The surest way to control it is to keep the noisy source far from the people it would disturb, so siting industries away from residential areas is the best measure. Planning laws can also separate airports, factories and busy roads from housing.

  • Complete combustion of fuel reduces smoke and gases, which is air-pollution control.
  • Planting trees along roads muffles some sound, but it only reduces noise that is already there.
  • Wearing ear devices protects one person's hearing without lowering the noise.

Removing the source from homes is the most effective control.

question: A constituent of the exhaust fumes from electricity generating sets which causes serious pollution is
solution:
Generating sets burn petrol or diesel, and when the fuel burns without enough oxygen it forms carbon(II) oxide (CO). This gas is colourless and odourless but very dangerous: it binds to haemoglobin in the blood far more strongly than oxygen does, so the blood carries less oxygen and the body's cells are starved, causing headache, unconsciousness and even death.

  • Water vapour is harmless.
  • Carbon(IV) oxide is a normal product of complete combustion and mainly a greenhouse gas.
  • Ozone is not released directly in exhaust fumes.

Carbon(II) oxide is therefore the serious pollutant meant here.

question: Which of the following is true of smallpox?

option.b: It can effectively be controlled with antibiotics
option.c: It can effectively be controlled by vaccination

solution:
Smallpox is caused by the variola virus and spreads through droplets from the mouth and nose, or by contact with infected material. The true statement is that it can effectively be controlled by vaccination: the vaccine, made from the related cowpox virus, gave lasting protection.

  • It is not transmitted by bacteria.
  • Antibiotics kill bacteria, not viruses, so they cannot control smallpox.
  • It is not a water-borne infection like cholera or typhoid.

Vaccination was so successful that smallpox became the first human disease to be completely eradicated.

question: A pollutant that is mostly associated with acid rain is
solution:
Acid rain forms when pollutant gases dissolve in rain water to make acids. Nitrogen(IV) oxide (NO2), released from vehicle engines and power stations, reacts with water and oxygen in the air to form nitric acid, which falls in rain and damages leaves, soils, lakes and buildings.

  • Ozone is a secondary pollutant that harms the lungs but is not the main acid-rain gas.
  • Fluorine is a reactive element, not a common acid-rain pollutant.
  • Carbon(IV) oxide forms only weakly acidic carbonic acid.

Sulphur(IV) oxide acts in the same way but is not listed, so nitrogen(IV) oxide is the answer.

question: When the adults have reached a certain degree of weakness, the process of binary fission is replaced by conjugation in
solution:
Paramecium normally multiplies asexually by transverse binary fission, one cell splitting across into two. If this is repeated many times, the offspring become weak and their vigour falls. The organism then uses conjugation, a sexual process in which two Paramecia join and exchange micronuclear material, restoring vitality and producing new gene combinations.

Amoeba and Euglena simply divide by fission and do not conjugate. Plasmodium does have a sexual stage, but it takes place inside the mosquito gut and is not a replacement for fission in a weakened adult. The description therefore fits Paramecium.

question: Whorls, arches, loops and composites are types of variation in
solution:
Variations are differences between individuals of the same species. The ridge patterns on the skin of the fingertips — arches, loops, whorls and composites — are inherited features used in fingerprint identification, because the arrangement differs from person to person.

Colour of skin, hair colour and blood group are also variations, but the four terms given do not describe them. Blood groups are named A, B, AB and O, and colour differences are described as shades, not whorls or loops. These terms belong specifically to dermatoglyphics, the study of skin ridge patterns.

question: A couple has 10 children, all female. Which of the following best explains the situation?

option.a: The sex determination was by the man's X chromosome
option.b: The man's sperm count is low
option.c: The woman is not capable of producing male children
option.d: The sex determination was by the man's Y chromosome

solution:
Sex in humans is decided by the sex chromosomes. A woman has XX, so every egg carries an X. A man has XY, so his sperms are of two kinds: half carry X and half carry Y.

A child is female when an X-bearing sperm fertilises the egg (XX) and male when a Y-bearing sperm does (XY). If all ten children are girls, then on each occasion the fertilising sperm carried an X, so sex determination was by the man's X chromosome. This is a matter of chance, not of low sperm count, and the mother's eggs cannot by themselves produce a male. A Y chromosome would have produced boys.

question: A biological agent with antiviral property is
solution:
When a cell is infected by a virus it releases a protein called interferon. This does not attack the virus directly; instead it makes neighbouring cells resistant, so that the virus cannot multiply inside them. This gives the body a first line of defence while specific antibodies are being produced.

  • Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up reactions.
  • Antibiotics act on bacteria and are useless against viruses.
  • Disinfectants are chemicals used on objects, not agents made by the body.

Interferon is therefore the biological agent with antiviral property.

question: One of the advantages of outbreeding is
solution:
Outbreeding, or cross-breeding, means mating individuals from different and unrelated breeds or varieties. The offspring are heterozygous for many genes, a condition called hybrid vigour or heterosis. Such offspring are usually stronger and more resistant to disease, because harmful recessive alleles from one parent are masked by healthy dominant alleles from the other.

Inbreeding, by contrast, makes organisms more homozygous and can expose genetic defects. Pest tolerance, fast growth and tall height may sometimes occur, but the well-established advantage of outbreeding is improved health and disease resistance, so that option is correct.

question: An individual with blood group AB can receive blood from those in blood group(s)
solution:
Blood group depends on antigens on the red cells and antibodies in the plasma. A person of group AB has both A and B antigens on the red cells, so the plasma contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies. With no antibodies to clump the incoming cells, an AB person can safely receive blood of groups A, B, AB and O, and is called the universal recipient.

  • Group O has no A or B antigens, so it can be given to anyone.
  • Groups A, B and AB each carry antigens that an AB recipient tolerates.

Limiting the answer to AB only, or to A and B only, would wrongly exclude compatible donors.

question: The streamlined shape of fishes is an adaptation for
solution:
Fishes have a streamlined body, rounded at the head and tapering to the tail, which lets water flow smoothly past them. This reduces the resistance, or drag, of the water so the fish can swim with little effort, escape enemies and travel to feeding grounds.

Other adaptations help: overlapping scales and mucus reduce friction further, while fins and a muscular tail provide propulsion and steering. The streamlined shape does not by itself help in securing mates, obtaining food or attacking and defending, although easier movement may assist the fish in doing those things. Its direct purpose is easy movement through water.

question: All living organisms are constantly involved in a struggle for existence. This was proposed by
solution:
The idea that living things face a constant struggle for existence — competing for food, space and mates while escaping predators and disease — was put forward by Charles Darwin. He argued that individuals with useful variations survive and reproduce, while others fail, and this is the process of natural selection.

Lamarck proposed the use and disuse of body parts instead. Wallace also wrote about evolution, but the phrase “struggle for existence” is associated with Darwin’s book On the Origin of Species. Morgan studied heredity in fruit flies, not this idea. The correct answer is Darwin.

question: A tissue is composed of a group of
solution: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to do one particular job. Muscle tissue, for example, is made of many muscle cells that look alike and contract as one. Cells are the smallest unit of life, so a tissue must be built from cells, not from other tissues, organs or systems. Groups of different tissues working together form an organ (such as the stomach). Organs working together form a system (such as the digestive system), and systems build the whole organism. This shows that the other options are levels above a tissue, so they cannot be what a tissue is made of.

question: The population of different organisms that exist together in a habitat is called
solution: This question asks for the name given to all the different populations living together in one place. A community is made up of every organism that shares a habitat and interacts there: grasses, insects, lizards, birds and micro-organisms on a school field, for example. A population is only one kind of organism, so it is smaller than a community. A biome is a very large region such as a savannah or desert, a biosphere is all the living parts of the earth together, and ecology is the study of how organisms relate to their surroundings, not the group of organisms itself.

question: Which of the following serves as the brain box in man?
solution: The 'brain box' is the bony case that encloses and protects the soft brain. In humans this case is the skull, whose upper and back part, the cranium, forms a hard box round the brain and shields it from knocks, just as a helmet protects a footballer's head. The skeleton is the whole framework of bones in the body, which is far too broad an answer. The head is a general word covering the face, eyes and skin as well as the bones. The spinal column is the line of bones that protects the spinal cord, not the brain.

question: Which organ removes the largest amount of excess water from the body?
solution: Water leaves the body in urine, in sweat and as water vapour in the breath, but the kidneys remove the largest share. Each day the kidneys filter the whole blood supply many times, taking out urea, excess salts and surplus water to form urine, which flows to the bladder. That is about one and a half litres of water lost daily as urine, more than is lost through sweat or breathing. The liver breaks down harmful substances but removes little water, the lungs mainly remove carbon dioxide, and the skin loses water in sweat but in a smaller amount.

question: A group of organisms of the same kind inhabiting the same environment is called
solution: A population is a group of organisms of the same kind (the same species) living together in the same environment at the same time and able to breed with one another. All the mango trees in a compound, or all the tilapia in a pond, form one population. A species is the group of similar organisms that can interbreed, but a species is not tied to one particular place. A habitat is the place where the organisms live, and an ecosystem is that habitat together with all its living things. The key words in the question are 'same kind' and 'same environment', which together define a population.

question: The light-sensitive cells in the human eye are called
solution: The eye contains light-sensitive cells called rods and cones. Cones are the photoreceptor cells that respond to bright light and let us see colour, while rods work in dim light. Because cones are individual cells containing light-absorbing pigments, they fit the description 'light-sensitive cells' in the question. The retina is the layer or sheet that holds these cells, so it is the place where they lie rather than the cells themselves. The choroid is a dark, blood-rich layer that nourishes the eye, and the sclerotic layer is the tough white outer coat that protects the eyeball.

question: The earliest form of life in the animal kingdom is the
solution: Among the vertebrate classes, fish (Pisces) appeared first. They were the earliest animals with a backbone and lived entirely in water, breathing with gills. Amphibians came next, able to live partly on land, then reptiles, then birds and finally mammals. Fossils of fish-like vertebrates are far older than those of amphibians, and the other groups appear even later in the rocks. This is why Aves (birds), Amphibia and Reptilia are all more recent. The usual order is Pisces → Amphibia → Reptilia → Aves → Mammalia, so Pisces is the earliest of the four listed.

question: Which of the following diseases is not sexually transmitted?
solution: Sexually transmitted infections pass mainly from person to person during sexual contact. Gonorrhoea (a bacterium), herpes (a virus) and syphilis (a bacterium) are all spread in this way, so they are not the answer. Influenza, or flu, is a virus infection of the breathing passages. It spreads through tiny droplets in the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes, or by touching a contaminated surface and then the mouth or nose. A person can therefore catch flu without any sexual contact at all, which makes it the disease that is not sexually transmitted.

question: Which of the following is not a monocotyledonous seed?
solution: Flowering plants are divided into monocotyledons, whose seeds have one cotyledon (seed leaf), and dicotyledons, whose seeds have two. Maize, millet and wheat are grasses, and each of their grains contains a single cotyledon, so they are monocotyledonous. Cowpea is a legume; a soaked cowpea splits into two halves, showing two cotyledons, its leaves have network veins and its seedling produces two seed leaves, all dicot features. Cowpea is therefore the seed that is not monocotyledonous. You can check this at home by soaking a bean and a grain of maize.

question: The lowest unit of classification is the
solution: Living things are grouped from the largest to the smallest taxon: kingdom → phylum → class → order → family → genus → species. Species is the lowest and smallest unit because it contains organisms that resemble one another closely and can interbreed to produce fertile offspring. A genus is one step above species and groups closely related species. A class and a phylum are much larger groups that contain many families. Humans, for instance, are Homo sapiens, where Homo is the genus and sapiens the species. Nothing smaller than a species is used in classification.

question: One of the following diseases is caused by fungi.
solution: Fungal diseases of plants often show as rust-coloured or powdery patches and spots on leaves. Coffee leaf rust is caused by a fungus that grows on coffee leaves, producing yellow-orange spots that reduce photosynthesis and lower the harvest. The other options are caused by viruses: cassava mosaic, tomato mosaic and cassava rosette are viral diseases spread by sap-sucking insects or through infected cuttings. Viruses are much smaller than fungi and cannot be seen with the naked eye. So the only fungal disease listed is coffee leaf rust. Remember that rusts, mildews and many blights of crops are fungal.

question: The by-product of photosynthesis is
solution:
In photosynthesis, green plants use light energy trapped by chlorophyll to combine carbon dioxide and water into glucose, and oxygen is released as a by-product:

6CO2+6H2O→C6H12O6+6O2

Carbon dioxide and water are the raw materials taken in, so they are reactants, not by-products. Glucose (C6H12O6) is the main useful product, which the plant stores as starch. The oxygen given off is not needed for this reaction, so it is the by-product; it leaves through the stomata and is the gas animals need for respiration.

question: Gaseous exchange in the lungs takes place in the
solution: Gaseous exchange means oxygen passing from the air into the blood and carbon dioxide passing from the blood into the air. This happens in the alveoli, the millions of tiny air sacs at the ends of the bronchioles. Their walls are only one cell thick and are wrapped in a network of capillaries, so gases diffuse across quickly over a very large total surface area. The trachea (windpipe), bronchi and bronchioles are only tubes that carry air to and from the lungs. Their walls are thicker and have no rich blood supply for exchange, so exchange does not take place there.

question: In eukaryotic cells, cellular respiration takes place in the
solution: Cellular respiration is the breakdown of food such as glucose to release energy. In eukaryotic cells the main part of this happens in the mitochondria, which are called the power houses of the cell. Using oxygen, they break glucose down into carbon dioxide and water and store the released energy in ATP molecules. A small first stage does occur in the cytoplasm, but the greatest amount of energy is produced inside the mitochondrion, so it is the best answer. The nucleus holds DNA and controls the cell, and centrioles help during cell division; neither releases energy from food.

question: Which of the following causes Ebola fever?
solution: Ebola fever is a severe haemorrhagic fever caused by the Ebola virus. Viruses are not true cells; they can multiply only inside a living host cell, and this one spreads through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person. Bacteria are single-celled organisms that cause diseases such as cholera and tuberculosis. Fungi cause ringworm and athlete's foot, and protozoa cause malaria and sleeping sickness. None of these causes Ebola. Knowing the type of pathogen matters for treatment, because antibiotics act on bacteria but have no effect on viruses.

question: The theory of survival of the fittest was propounded by
solution: The theory of the survival of the fittest was put forward by Charles Darwin. He explained that members of a species vary, and those with helpful features, such as better camouflage or faster running, are more likely to survive, breed and pass those features to their offspring. Over many generations the species becomes better adapted to its surroundings. Lamarck taught a different idea, that characteristics gained during an organism's life are inherited. Hooke is remembered for discovering cells with the microscope, and Linnaeus for the system of naming and classifying organisms.

question: The deficiency of vitamin D leads to
solution: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and phosphate from food and use them to harden bones and teeth. When it is lacking, the bones of a growing child stay soft and bend under the body's weight, giving bow legs, a deformed chest and delayed closing of the soft spot on the head; this condition is rickets. Sunlight falling on the skin makes vitamin D, and it is also found in fish liver oil and egg yolk. Beriberi is caused by lack of vitamin B1, pellagra by lack of niacin, and scurvy by lack of vitamin C, which causes bleeding gums.

question: One of these is used for excretion in the earthworm.
solution: Excretion is the removal of waste products made inside the body. In the earthworm the excretory organs are the nephridia, tiny coiled tubes found in most body segments. Each nephridium collects wastes such as ammonia and urea from the body fluid, returns useful substances to the body, and passes the urine out through a small pore in the skin. Contractile vacuoles remove surplus water from single-celled organisms like Amoeba. Flame cells are the excretory organs of flatworms such as the tapeworm, and Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects, opening into the gut.

question: The following group of plants is the most advanced except
solution: Plant groups can be arranged from the simplest to the most advanced: thallophytes → bryophytes (mosses) → pteridophytes (ferns) → spermatophytes (seed plants). Thallophytes have a flat, undifferentiated body with no true roots, stems or leaves and no conducting tissues, so they are the least advanced. Bryophytes have simple leaf-like parts but no vascular tissue, and pteridophytes have true vascular tissue but no seeds. Spermatophytes are the most developed because they bear seeds and flowers. The question asks for the group that is not advanced, so the answer is the thallophytic group.

question: Which of the following hormonal glands is located on top of the kidney?
solution: The adrenal glands sit like caps on top of the two kidneys. Each has an outer cortex, which makes hormones such as cortisol and aldosterone, and an inner medulla, which makes adrenaline. Adrenaline prepares the body for action in danger, while aldosterone helps to balance salts and water in the blood. The gonads (testes and ovaries) lie in the scrotum or lower abdomen, the pancreas lies behind the stomach, and the thyroid gland is in the neck around the windpipe. The position given in the question, on top of the kidney, identifies the adrenal gland.

question: One of these is present in both plant and animal cells?
